name: @examples/probe-proving-cases
//dependencies: The two packages #16's fifth acceptance criterion requires to be evaluated
end to end: one simple ESM package and one Worker/WASM-risk package. Both are
installed from npm at an exact version, never a range, because the probe's
evidence is about *this* published artifact — a range that could resolve
differently would silently change what was measured, and the whole point of the
criterion is that the verdict rests on a real artifact rather than on packaging
the evaluator wrote itself.
`es-toolkit` is the simple case. It is also the package `#10`'s PoC already
proved inlineable end to end (examples/inline-es-toolkit +
packages/cell-compiler/src/inline-es-toolkit-poc.test.ts), which makes a
rejection of it self-evidently wrong rather than a judgement call.
`@embedpdf/pdfium` is the Worker/WASM-risk case, and it is the package #16's own
"Example policy: PDF" section names: "Do not default to low-level pdfjs-dist
merely because it is famous. The Agent should compare higher-level modern
browser/React alternatives (for example an EmbedPDF-style package), probe actual
WASM/Worker/asset behavior". Choosing it keeps the proving case an instance of
the Spec's policy rather than a counter-example to it. It ships a 4.6 MB
`pdfium.wasm` and resolves it through `new URL('pdfium.wasm', import.meta.url)`,
which is exactly the shape that must surface as a *risk* to be weighed rather
than as an automatic rejection.
Neither package is imported by any cell in this repository. The dependency exists
so the probe has a real installed artifact to measure, and the probe is run from
this package's directory so Node resolution anchors where the packages are
declared.
